title: Finite type relation kernels in an extension of coherent modules
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $0\to\mathcal F_1\to\mathcal F_2\to\mathcal F_3\to0$ be a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $\mathcal F_1$ and $\mathcal F_3$ coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. For every open $U\subseteq X$, every integer $n\geq0$ and every morphism $g:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F_2|_U$, the sheaf $\operatorname{Ker}g$ is of finite type, meaning locally generated by finitely many sections.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BY (lemma-coherent-abelian), proof of (4), relation-kernel diagram

proof.text: Restrict S to U with SheafOfModules.overFunctor. Its existing finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation instances give ShortExact.map_of_exact. Set q = g followed by the restricted last map. The relation clause of coherence of the last term, applied directly at U to q, says kernel q is finite type. No separate coherence-restriction theorem is needed here.

Apply ShortExact.fIsKernel to the restricted sequence. The composite kernel q -> free -> middle term is killed by the last map, so it factors uniquely as phi : kernel q -> first term. Construct kernel phi -> kernel g by composing the two kernel inclusions and lifting into kernel g. Conversely, lift kernel g -> free into kernel q, then into kernel phi: its composite with phi is zero after the monic first map, hence zero. Cancellation of the three kernel inclusions proves the two lifts are inverse. This is the private extension_kernel_iso proof, using no snake lemma.

Apply the open-slice finite type kernel lemma to phi, whose source kernel q is finite type and whose target is the restriction of the coherent first term. Transport finite local generating families along kernel phi isomorphic to kernel g: keep the same cover and finite indexing sets, and compose each local free epimorphism with the restricted isomorphism. Epimorphisms and finiteness are preserved, giving the required finite type kernel.
